title: Review: in town
why: Review of the "In Town" unit: directions, prepositions with the article, verbs of movement, and polite phrases, all brought together on a bus ride in Jerusalem. It wraps up level A1 before the past tense.

Finding your way in town

To…HebrewPronunciation
ask whereסְלִיחָה, אֵיפֹה הַתַּחֲנָה?slikha, eifo ha-takhana?
look for any place of a kindיֵשׁ פֹּה בַּנְק?yesh po bank?
give directionsיָשָׁר, וְאָז יָמִינָה / שְׂמֹאלָהyashar, ve'az yamina / smola
say where something isלְיַד הַשּׁוּקleyad ha-shuk
talk about distanceקָרוֹב / רָחוֹק, חָמֵשׁ דַּקּוֹת בָּרֶגֶלkarov / rakhok, khamesh dakot ba-regel

And the prepositions with the article: בַּ (in the), לַ (to the, toward the), מֵהַ (from the). בַּתַּחֲנָה, לַתַּחֲנָה, מֵהַתַּחֲנָה.

Remember: אֵיפֹה = where you are, לְאָן = where you're going, מֵאֵיפֹה = where you're coming from.

To ask politely: אֶפְשָׁר…? (can I…?), תּוּכַל / תּוּכְלִי…? (could you…?), and the set phrases תַּגִּיד / תַּגִּידִי, תָּבוֹא / תָּבוֹאִי, תְּחַכֶּה / תְּחַכִּי רֶגַע.

תּוּכַל לְהַגִּיד לִי מָתַי לָרֶדֶת?Could you tell me when to get off? (to a man) [tukhal lehagid li matai laredet?]
", "

On a Jerusalem bus

Two names you need to get around Jerusalem. They are nouns followed by an adjective, with the article on both words, like הַבַּיִת הַגָּדוֹל:

הַתַּחֲנָה הַמֶּרְכָּזִיתthe central bus station [ha-takhana ha-merkazit]
הָרַכֶּבֶת הַקַּלָּהthe light rail (\"the light train\") [ha-rakevet ha-kala]
אֵיזֶה קַו נוֹסֵעַ לַתַּחֲנָה הַמֶּרְכָּזִית?Which line goes to the central bus station? [eize kav nose'a la-takhana ha-merkazit?]

Usually you get on at the front, tap your רַב־קַו near the driver, and don't hesitate to ask the driver to let you know: תּוּכַל לְהַגִּיד לִי?

If you don't know where to get off, ask the person next to you: סְלִיחָה, הַשּׁוּק בַּתַּחֲנָה הַבָּאָה? (excuse me, is the market at the next stop?). Israelis love to help, often several at once!
